Maybe growing together is not becoming less annoying. Maybe it is learning which small things are only small things—and which ones are asking us to stay close.

Send this to the person you still want to take on the date, even when the plan fails. 🤍
caption_alt: Not a love without small fights. A love that learns what they are really about—and still stops for chai.
alt_text: Illustrated carousel slide 1: FLASH-FORWARD COVER, one continuous physical scene and decisive choice. Wide diagonal view of the fixed rain-damp service-lane geography. Exactly Aachu and Zuv stand full-length at the same depth beside the single charcoal compact sedan, safely parked parallel to the quieter curb with its silver five-spoke rear wheel and small red rear-light wedge visible. Across the divided road, the fixed warm terracotta restaurant doorway with muted sage awning is visibly close but awkward to reach; it has no sign, letters, menu, staff, diners, silhouettes, or reflections. Beside the couple, the fixed narrow blue-grey chai counter with rust-red canopy and EXACTLY TWO EMPTY dark-wood stools waits with no vendor, cups, food, or signage. Aachu has taken one visible step toward the two stools: her feet and torso move stall-ward, her right hand gives one open-palm invitation toward those stools, and her left hand visibly supports the strap of her red handbag on her own left shoulder. Zuv turns the route phone inward in his left hand and has begun one visible following step behind her, looking at Aachu rather than the screen. The diagonal movement must read without copy as: the original plan failed and they are actively choosing the smaller date together. The fixed deep-navy umbrella remains closed against the car. No chai has been served. No touch, generic standing pose, scooter, motorbike, helmet, road sign, random lettering, or extra person.
